issuer: South Carolina Advisory Committee on Standards of Judicial Conduct (Supreme Court of South Carolina)
title: Advisory Opinion No. 01-2025: Propriety of a Circuit Court judge serving on a board to award a small scholarship to student who is enrolled in a college, university, or tech school pursuing an undergraduate degree in Legal Studies or seeking a Paralegal Certificate.
text:
ADVISORY COMMITTEE
ON STANDARDS OF JUDICIAL CONDUCT
OPINION NO. 1 - 2025
RE:
Propriety of a Circuit Court judge serving on a board to award a small scholarship to student
who is enrolled in a college, university, or tech school pursuing an undergraduate degree
in Legal Studies or seeking a Paralegal Certificate.
FACTS
A Circuit Court Judge has been contacted by a member of Legal Staff Professionals of
South Carolina (“LSPSC”), a group of members who work in law firms and other legal entities as
administrative people. The organization is an affiliate of the National Association for Legal
Professionals.  The member is the chair of the 2025 Scholarship Committee. LSPSC awards
annually a $1,500 scholarship to a deserving student who is enrolled in a college,  university, or
tech school pursuing an undergraduate degree in Legal Studies or seeking a Paralegal Certificate.
The award will be made in April 2025 at the annual education conference.  The Scholarship
Committee is seeking three people to view applications and rank them: A judge, a teacher, and a
community leader.  The Scholarship Committee has asked the judge to participate.
The Scholarship Committee will send the judge the applications for review. The judge
would then rank them based on the criteria/qualifications. There are usually only a small number
of applications so the reviewing process would not interfere with the judge’s judicial duties.
CONCLUSION
A Circuit Court judge may serve on a selection committee for a scholarship given by the
LSPSC.
OPINION
A judge shall conduct all of the judge's extrajudicial activities so that they do not cast
reasonable doubt on the judge's capacity to act impartially as a judge. Rule 501, Canon 4(A) (1),

SCACR. A judge may serve as officer, director, trustee or non-legal advisor of an education
organization not conducted for profit. Rule 501, Canon 4(C)(3), SCACR. In Opinion 13-2000, we
addressed a similar question as the one presented here.  There, we found that a Circuit Court judge
could serve on a selection committee for a scholarship given at the University of South Carolina
School of Law. We determined that  the scholarship selection committee is a nonprofit educational
organization and thus the judge could serve. We see no reason to deviate from that logic here.
Thus, the inquiring judge may participate in the ranking of scholarship applications for the LSPSC.
s/Usha Jeffries Bridges
USHA JEFFRIES BRIDGES, CHAIR
s/William H. Seals, Jr.
WILLIAM H. SEALS, JR.
s/Ariail E. King
February 13, 2025
ARIAIL E. KING
